title: Why Is There a Spider Web on a Steelpan?

voice_performance.performance_intent: Plain-spoken and warm, like showing a friend something clever. Not a lecture. Land the payoff, then ease off for the name.
voice_performance.energy_curve: curious open, steady build, small lift on 'rings clean', settle for the closing line
voice_performance.pause_policy: Short beat after the hook. Half-beat before 'they buzz'. Full beat before 'That's why'.

provider_notes.piper: en_US medium voice. Do not attempt a Trinidadian accent. Slight downward inflection on 'his drawing.'

sections.label: Hook
sections.text: That spider web on a steelpan? It's not a decoration. It's a map.
sections.speaker_directions: Curious, a little sly. Tiny pause before 'It's a map.'

enhancement_cues.description: A single web strand draws across the pan face, then the full web resolves

sections.label: Setup - one sheet of steel
sections.text: Every note sits on one piece of steel. Put two clashing notes next to each other, and they buzz. They fight through the metal.

enhancement_cues.description: Two note-blobs flash red side by side and visibly rattle
Faint distortion on the music bed under 'buzz'

sections.label: Build - the map splits them up
sections.text: So the map splits them up. Clashing notes go to opposite sides of the drum. Notes that sound good together sit close.

enhancement_cues.description: Red blobs slide apart to opposite edges and go quiet
Two blobs glow warm orange and snap next to each other

sections.label: Payoff
sections.text: That's why a steelpan rings clean instead of rattling. The pattern is the reason it sounds like that.
sections.speaker_directions: Small lift on 'rings clean'. This is the point - let it land.

enhancement_cues.description: Full pan diagram glows once, warm

sections.label: Landing - Williams + end tag
sections.text: A tuner named Anthony Williams worked this out in Trinidad, in 1953. Every lead pan in the world still follows his drawing.
sections.speaker_directions: Warm, proud, unhurried. Downward inflection on 'his drawing.'

enhancement_cues.description: The web pattern multiplies small across a faint world map
End tag composited on the final frame

guardrail_checks.contested_credit_stated_as_fact: pass - credits Williams with the 4ths-and-5ths spider-web LAYOUT (well established); does NOT touch the contested 55-gallon-oil-drum credit
guardrail_checks.on_screen_assets: pass - animated diagram + type only; no archival photos, no depiction of Williams
guardrail_checks.audio_rights: pass - music bed only, no pan performance recording

metadata.review_flag: The year 1953 is from secondary sources (Wikipedia, layout-history sites); the vetted Series 1 fact base names Williams but does not commit to a year. Confirm 1953 with a pan source before this is ever published, or soften to 'the early 1950s'.
